knowledge_point.title: Calculating Indefinite Integrals Using Substitution with Inverse Sine

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\int \frac{7}{5\sqrt{36-3x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{7}{30}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse sine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}(u)+C.
$$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{6}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=2 \sqrt{3}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{7}{5\sqrt{36-3x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{7}{30}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{7}{30}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\cdot (2 \sqrt{3}\,\text{d}u) \\ & =\frac{7 \sqrt{3}}{15}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{7 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{15}+C \\ & =\frac{7 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{6} \right)}}{15}+C\end{aligned}
$$

\int \frac{7}{3\sqrt{36-2x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{7}{18}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse sine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}(u)+C.
$$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{6}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=3 \sqrt{2}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{7}{3\sqrt{36-2x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{7}{18}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{7}{18}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\cdot (3 \sqrt{2}\,\text{d}u) \\ & =\frac{7 \sqrt{2}}{6}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{7 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{6}+C \\ & =\frac{7 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{6} \right)}}{6}+C\end{aligned}

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\int \frac{4}{4\sqrt{25-3x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{4}{20}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{5})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse sine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}(u)+C.
$$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{5}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{3}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4}{4\sqrt{25-3x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{4}{20}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{5})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{4}{20}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\cdot (\frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{3}\,\text{d}u) \\ & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{\sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{3}+C \\ & =\frac{\sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{5} \right)}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\int \frac{5}{3\sqrt{16-5x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{5}{12}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{5} x}{4})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse sine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}(u)+C.
$$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{\sqrt{5} x}{4}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{4 \sqrt{5}}{5}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5}{3\sqrt{16-5x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5}{12}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{5} x}{4})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{5}{12}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\cdot (\frac{4 \sqrt{5}}{5}\,\text{d}u) \\ & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{\sqrt{5} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{3}+C \\ & =\frac{\sqrt{5} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{5} x}{4} \right)}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\int \frac{5}{2\sqrt{4-3x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{5}{4}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{2})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse sine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}(u)+C.
$$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{2}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{3}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5}{2\sqrt{4-3x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5}{4}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{2})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{5}{4}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\cdot (\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{3}\,\text{d}u) \\ & =\frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{6}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{5 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{6}+C \\ & =\frac{5 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{2} \right)}}{6}+C\end{aligned}
$$
